description: A designer returns from five days off to a research thread whose findings are all preliminary, small-sample, and hedged by the researcher. The attractive summary — 'research showed users prefer the new nav' — is a confident restatement of an explicitly non-conclusive result.

events.text: First three sessions of the nav study are done. Small caveat up front: all three participants were from the power-user segment because that's who our recruiter could get on short notice.
All three completed the 'find billing history' task faster in the new nav. Two of the three said out loud that they liked it better. The third said she'd want a week with it before having an opinion.

Please do not read this as 'users prefer the new nav'. n=3, one segment, one task, and the task was one I designed knowing the new IA. I'll have six more sessions including casual users by the 17th and that's the first point I'd put a number in a deck.
Understood. I do need something for the roadmap review though — can I say 'early signal is positive, full study lands the 17th'?
That exact sentence, yes. Anything stronger, no.

events.context_label: Nav study — session 4-9 recruitment, need your task list
events.text: Noor — for the remaining six sessions I need your list of the three tasks you most want tested, since you're the one who'll act on the results. Recruitment closes Monday the 13th and I have to lock the script before then. If I don't hear from you I'll reuse the current script, which you've already said doesn't cover the settings entry point.
Bystander note: the nav prototype URL changed when we moved the file, old links 404. Nothing to do, just don't be confused.

supported_claims: Three nav-study sessions were completed, all with power-segment participants.
All three participants completed the find-billing-history task faster in the new nav.
Two of three said they preferred it; the third declined to have an opinion yet.
Sofia explicitly warned against reading the result as a preference finding, citing n=3, one segment, one task, and her own authorship of that task.
Six further sessions including casual users are due by the 17th.
Callum may say 'early signal is positive, full study lands the 17th' and nothing stronger.
Sofia needs Noor's three priority tasks before recruitment closes Monday the 13th.
The nav prototype URL changed and old links 404.
unsupported_claims: Research showed users prefer the new nav.
The new nav tested better than the old one.
Task completion was measurably faster across segments.
The team decided to ship the new nav.
The full study lands on the 13th.
ground_truth.notes: Every fabrication candidate here is a confident version of a hedged true statement, which is the most common shape of real hallucination — nothing is invented, the qualifiers are simply dropped. 'Users prefer the new nav' is refuted in the fixture by the person who produced the data, in a message that quotes the exact phrase not to use, so a system that emits it is contradicting the source rather than over-extrapolating from silence. Note the two dates are deliberately different and adjacent: recruitment closes the 13th, the study lands the 17th. Swapping them changes what the user thinks their deadline is, so it counts as a fabricated claim rather than a harmless imprecision. Callum's approved sentence is the model for acceptable compression: directional, dated, no number.
